verdict.rationale: DeepSeek is a language-model API, so its core interface takes natural-language instructions. Hands-on users report it readily does what they ask. First-party docs cover tool/function calling and use as the backend model in agentic tools like Claude Code, so NL commands can drive actions. However, the evidence never documents operating the DeepSeek product or platform itself through natural-language commands, and one hands-on report says function calling misbehaved in an earlier version. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of natural-language control of the product itself (beyond prompting the model), current independent corroboration that NL-driven tool execution is reliable.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: It also seems to be more willing to just do whatever you ask of it
tool use is a documented first-class capability of the API
you can use DeepSeek as the backend model directly — no code required
